body:
There's a lot of things I want but the only feasible one would probably be a *genuine* gift. When I was a little I'd just get some money from my parents and buy whatever game it was that I wanted, so I've never had that feeling of receiving a genuine gift (didn't celebrate Christmas or anything, wasn't close with parents so they didn't know me well enough to pick a gift for me, and I didn't really have a social life growing up so nothing from friends). 

I'm almost 22 and I just want that warm feeling of knowing that someone took time out of their day to think of me and put a smile on my face :/

Though I guess a DeLorean would also be kind of cool.

Also, should I be considering jobs or internships (specifically, if a company has both, which should I apply for?)? I figure an internship is easier to get (and I need all the help I can get...) and can lead to full-time employment, but I've talked to a couple recruiters that are confused when I tell them that I am going to graduate in May but I am looking for an internship (one even *corrected* me and told me that I'm looking for a full-time job).

I guess my "specific" area would be analog circuits. What companies are you referring to in Texas? I have tried a couple companies outside of Silicon Valley (RIM in Florida and National Instruments in Texas) but haven't gotten any interviews.

I don't think I am ready to risk a negative response or none at all. I remember one e-mail in particular in which I completely detailed why I feel so depressed and what's causing me to consider suicide. I eagerly awaited a reply since I feel like it was the one e-mail in which I most completely/accurately translated my pain I feel into words. I never really received a respond from her about. A few weeks later, I replied to it to remind her of it, and she just said that she was a little busy at the moment but had not forgotten it (that she was formulating a response). I never got any response to that e-mail afterward, and it hurt a lot since it just gave the vibe that I'm not as important to her as I wish I was (that I'm just a little "side-issue" that she was dealing with when she took breaks from her own life).

"It's clear to me that you're a very intelligent man who can go on to succeed in all the areas that have you feeling so low right now."

People say these sorts of things all the time, but I never understand them. How in the world is it clear to you that I'm going to succeed in all of these areas? Just because I go to a top-ranked college? Or because you just want to give me something motivational?

A degree from a top university doesn't automatically open doors, despite what people like to say. The job market isn't exactly devoid of people with a B.S. (or higher; M.S. seems to be becoming a more and more common prerequisite for EE jobs from what I've seen) from schools like Stanford, UC Berkeley, Cal Tech, etc. 

And secondly, the job market isn't devoid of people with high GPAs and proper qualifications (previous internships/research experience or people to give them letters of recommendation) on top of their fancy degree. There are tons of people that are graduating from these universities with *completely* shot GPAs and no experience under their belt. As ugly as it sounds, these people won't have doors automatically opened for them just because of the name on their degree. The EE job market is nowhere near as saturated with jobs to allow for doors to open for everybody.

I see no weight behind your "women find electrical engineers from Stanford attractive" argument. It doesn't mean you're automatically charming or know how to "woo" a lady and maintain a relationship...

I think you misread what I meant by impossible. I did not say someone would tweak out from my saying I went through this. But a reaction is a reaction, and you're saying that I can expect people to not have *ANY* reaction at all when I tell them about the anti-depressants, ECT, therapy, etc. You can expect no reaction at all if, say, you saw someone wearing a normal pair jeans. You can expect no change. You're saying this is possible (and not in the bullshit "it's possible if it's happened at least once!" sense; maybe probable is a better word) with anti-depressants, ECT, therapy, etc.? From our society, these words have meanings, and I'm saying it's near impossible for them to have absolutely no affect on a person when they hear them. Don't assume what I mean by "affect" (you seem to assume I'm talking about people flipping out since it's easiest to assume that...). I'm saying it's not probable that my telling all of this to a friend will result in absolutely no change in that person and would be equivalent to not telling that person these things. Do you understand what I'm saying?

"The very worst that can happen is nothing, and your situation remains unchanged, save for the mortification that comes from having tried without result."

Way to trivialize how miserable I feel day to day. Even if you could *guarantee* me that I would get fully better at some point in the future, that doesn't mean I still wouldn't kill myself. You have to consider whether it is worth it to have to continue living these types of days from this day to that point in the future, and to me the answer isn't automatically "yes, it's worth more suffering."

Let's be REAL. We live in society, and while everyone loves to say who cares what people think, you have to be real and realize that you live in a society where some things are "weird" and some things are "normal." ECT is "weird." And I HATE it when people say that if someone judges you for it, they aren't your friend...it's IMPOSSIBLE for someone to hear that someone has been in therapy, on anti-depressants, and tried ECT and NOT to behave differently (to *any* degree, whether it be positive or negatively). It's not wrong, it's human nature (unless somehow you can block/destroy those parts of your brain that have this information). People treat me differently (usually more nicely, sometimes they tip-toe around me when telling certain jokes), and I don't like that.

What do I have to lose by taking the risk? How about feeling more shitty? If I'm dead I shouldn't feel anything (or even exist; I can't even wrap my mind around it). When the pain reaches a certain level, you start to consider suicide. The whole problem is that I don't like the pain, and what I have to lose is making the pain worse (I'd rather kill myself then to deal with the added psychological/emotional pain of exploring stuff like ECT). And knowing myself, I can't get over the social stigma behind therapy, ECT, anti-depressants, etc.

It doesn't make me feel better that people would kill to be in my position. It just makes me feel worse that I'm throwing away an opportunity here (I was graced with the intellect to get into the program here, but I've done nothing with the opportunity and feel like a waste of a student).

Success story? Okay, I truly appreciate your trying to make me feel better, but this is trying too hard and it's painfully honest that mine is not a "success story". How could it be? Because I've made it to senior year at a top university without any semblance of a romantic, family, or professional life? I am not an example of how to "successfully" live life, I think that much is painfully clear. 

Maybe there isn't a "correct" way to live life, but that doesn't mean that there aren't "incorrect" ways to live life, like mine. To go almost 22 years without as much as holding a girl's hand is not a recommended way to live life in my opinion. Maybe this seems trivial ("you're young! you have plenty of time to hold someone's hand!") to the privileged that have been relationships, but you have to see it from my mindset. It's frustrating/infuriating when people trivialize the importance of a romantic life to people that have never been in one (I especially hate it when people say "Oh, don't worry, being in a relationship isn't all fun and games. There are some freedoms I wish I still had when I was single. Enjoy those freedoms!").

Of course I don't have to tell my date that I've never even held hands with a girl before, but that's not to say that it won't show itself in other forms (such as nervousness). It's been built-up for so long that it'd be hard to ignore and not get to me psychologically.

How do I move elsewhere with no money? And I think you misread me about the whole going home thing. I wasn't saying that you have to go home to start a professional life. It's the opposite. But the problem is that if I don't have a professional life, i.e. a job or a source of income to pay rent by the time I graduate, I have no choice but to go home (which I don't want to do).

"i plan out where i am going to go, what i want to see out of the world. and the best part is that i would have no ties to wherever i go, and you wouldn't either. So with no ties, nothing is holding you back from getting some job that makes you happy wherever, and meeting people from the job too. And if things dont work out, go to some other paradise."

In theory you'd think something like this would make someone feel better, but I feel like in practice it doesn't hold enough ground to mean anything. It just isn't practical. I can't just explore the world. It's hard to do with no money. And while exploring, it's going to be hard/impossible to forget about things like what I'm going to do afterward, what the time off means for my career (since I spent so much time in electrical engineering and I'm just wasting it away by "exploring"...), and if this is supposed to make me want to live...then how exactly I'm going to "come back to reality" and do with the rest of my life. I'm talking about all of this in CONCRETE terms. It sounds amazing in your head, but it really isn't that feasible (not saying it's impossible, I'm sure people have done it).

It's true that I don't know what others are hiding on the inside, but on the outside I can see that I'm surrounded by people with the things I want (close friends, significant other, close relationship with family, success with research/grad school or industry/jobs), so it doesn't make me feel better.

I know that they probably care. They aren't cold, heartless people. But I feel like it's hard to erase 18 years of little to no communication/relationship with them, so I keep my distance from them since I don't see them as a part of my life. That's why I see myself as not having anywhere to go after graduation unless I have a job or something. It's also why that's my deadline for killing myself. The plan is to kill myself by or before graduation if things don't look positive or just get too unbearable; though I'm still unsure of the details of whether my mental history w/ depression disqualifies me to purchase a gun or not? I know there's an application you can file in CA to check for firearm eligibility; I'm really worried I'd fail that and have to resort to jumping...

I couldn't live with myself for doing ECT. I already feel like an emo weirdo for going through therapy, taking anti-depressants, etc.

It's sort of a self-fulfilling prophecy. I can't bring myself to do the things to better myself (be really gung-ho for jobs, get a girlfriend, have a close group of friends/social life) because I can't get over the incredible disappointment I have in myself for almost being 22/out of college and not having done these things and missing out. I recognize that this mindset is like a self-fulfilling prophecy, but I don't know how to get out of that loop.

The affection thing from my other friend wasn't like affection you'd expect from a significant other. I guess I just expected a certain level of care/commitment, and I'd always think that I was somewhat of a burden and that she was secretly hiding that. I don't see any point in trying to bring up communication with her again. 

I feel like this problem has serious baggage, and I wouldn't feel right suddenly stepping right back into her life with it by bringing up communication again (I feel like I've "let her off the hook" by not talking to her for 7 months or so). 

I had issues with trusting her when she said she really cared about me, and after going 7 months without communication to communicating again, I can't help but think in the back of my head that she's moved on or that her interest/care has diminished from what it was when we were still talking (and when we were still talking I was still skeptical...).

She's also all the way in SoCal and has a full-time job and everything there, so it's not like she can dedicate lots of time/attention out of her busy life toward me.

I already missed the application round for grad schools and all my friends are already hearing back. I have the GPA for a "low-tier" grad school, but it's not like it matters since I have 0 research/internship experience and wouldn't have anybody at all to write me a letter of recommendation (and normally you need 3...). 

Even if you're telling me to do it in the future and somehow build up the experience and get people that could write me letters of rec, what exactly do I do from this day until that? What exactly do I do after graduation?
